prose.def: The shoulder, the part of the body on which loads and burdens are carried.
prose.article: ὦμος simply means the shoulder, especially viewed as the body part used to bear loads. prose.def: A point, stretch, or right moment of time — most often a clock hour, but also a brief span, a significant moment, or a coming era.

prose.article: ὥρα is the everyday Greek word for an "hour," and that is how it reads in 86% of its 105 New Testament appearances, with the Berean Study Bible agreeing 99% of the time. It also stretches to mean a broader "time" or "moment" (about 11% of cases), as in "the time is coming" — and older lexica note it could even mean a natural season. In the Septuagint it most often stands in for the Hebrew word עֵת, the general word for "time."

prose.article: At its root ὡραῖος comes from ὥρα ("hour, season") and literally means "in season" or "ripe," which is exactly how it shows up in everyday Koine papyri — describing ripe fruits, preserved fish, and grape harvests. The one remaining case is the proper name of the temple's "Beautiful" Gate in Acts 3:10. In the Septuagint it appears 23 times across 13 books, translating several Hebrew words for beauty and pleasantness, including תֹּ֫אַר ("form, appearance") four times.
prose.caution: The word appears only 4 times in the New Testament, so its full range there rests on thin biblical evidence, though papyri and the Septuagint confirm the seasonal-to-beautiful sense.

prose.article: ὡς is one of the most common little words in the Greek New Testament, appearing 499 times in the Byzantine text, and it works mainly as a connector meaning "as" or "like."
